title: Differential attention pathway orchestrator and clock-steer for MIG cohorts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Reduce 95th/99th token-latency and tail variance for mixed-SKU MIG deployments by dynamically choosing attention execution paths and coordinating per-slice clocking windows during prefill+decode. This ticket implements a runtime orchestration layer (Pathway Orchestrator) that: 1) selects among attention implementations (fused attention, tiled GEMM-based, sparse-aware paths) based on sequence length, token-density, and KV-cache heat; 2) coordinates transient clock-steer windows for MIG cohorts to unlock short bursts of headroom without violating thermal policies; and 3) integrates with existing telemetry to feedback real-time kernel-choice signals and fallback rules.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-token-latency reduced by >=12% for mixed H100/L40S workloads with 90-1024 seq distribution in lab benchmarks
No regressions (>1%) in median latency or throughput for isolated single-sku A10 workloads
Pathway Orchestrator chooses stable kernel paths for >=99% of requests in production canaries without causing increased OOMs or KV-cache thrashing
Clock-steer windows applied only when thermal headroom is >=15% and revert automatically on heater/telemetry anomalies
All changes behind a runtime feature flag and can be rolled back via Console rollout UI
implementation_steps: Add lightweight kernel-selection API in runtime shim that accepts sequence_length, token_density, kv_cache_hit_rate, and model_family
Implement a heuristics table and ML-lite scorer to rank candidate attention paths per request class
Wire clock-steer controller to MIG slice manager with per-slice short-lived governor requests and a safety watchdog
Expose selection decisions and clock actions as structured telemetry (trace spans + metric labels) and create dashboard in Console
Create canary rollout plan: lab -> internal staging -> 5% prod slice -> 25% -> full with automatic rollback thresholds
Add unit/integration tests covering choices across H100/L40S/A10 permutations and sequence length buckets
Document operator knobs (max_clock_boost_ms, min_thermal_headroom_pct, fallback_order) in runtime config docs
decisions: Use rule-based heuristics initially with a lightweight gradient-boosted scorer for later tuning instead of a full RL approach to limit risk and complexity
Clock-steer will be additive and transient (sub-second windows) and not modify persistent CUDA clocks to avoid cross-tenant drift
Default kernel preference for very short sequences (<32) is fused-attn; for long sequences (>512) prefer tiled-GEMM fallback unless KV-cache hit rate > 70%
All kernel switches are async and must ensure KV cache consistency; decoder path prefers ‘steady’ kernel when prefill-to-decode transition occurs within 200ms window
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased decision logic complexity can add micro-latency to hotpath — mitigated by caching decisions per route and sequence-bucket
Clock boosts may increase power draw and thermal cycling; mitigated with short windows and telemetry safeguards
Misclassification of request class could cause throughput regressions; plan includes guardrail thresholds and gradual rollout
Cross-sku behavior in mixed fleets is hard to reproduce in lab; depend on expanded fleet canaries in staging
notes: Initial lab benchmarking done on h100-l40s co-located cluster (run id: lab-2026-02-28) — saw median unchanged, tails improved in SET-A workloads
We observed a KV-cache churn pattern when naive kernel switching happened mid-request; solution: sticky kernel binding for prefill->decode transitions for 200ms
Found that A10 single-sku instances are sensitive to aggressive tiling; added safe thresholds to avoid throughput loss
Telemetry tag 'pathway.v1' added to traces to allow offline analysis and model retraining of scorer
testing_plan: Create synthetic request mixes that emulate conversational and long-document workloads across seq buckets [8,32,128,512,1024]
Run soak tests for 72h on mixed MIG cluster with automated rollback triggers on error rate >0.5% or latency regression >10%
Run A/B in staging with 1k concurrent users on dedicated pool to confirm no memory regressions
Add e2e perf tests into CI that assert pathway selection latency < 300us per decision
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged merge to runtime main and build runtime-1.23-rc1
Deploy to internal staging pool (24h) -> safety review -> enable 5% prod slice for 48h
Monitor custom dashboard and automated alerts; if stable increase to 25% for 72h, then full rollout
Post-rollout 2-week watch with retrospective doc and perf regression checks
